questions.prompt: Which URL pattern does clerkMiddleware protect in src/middleware.ts?

options.text: All routes except /api and /trpc
Only /dashboard(.*)
/dashboard(.*) and /checkout(.*)
Every route that is not a static asset

questions.explanation: createRouteMatcher(['/dashboard(.*)']) at src/middleware.ts line 3 matches only paths under /dashboard. The matcher config (lines 16-18) covers all pages and API routes but the protect() call is conditional — it only fires when isProtectedRoute(req) is true. Checkout, lobby, and API routes are all public.

evidence.note: isProtectedRoute pattern and conditional protect() call

questions.prompt: When an unauthenticated user hits /dashboard/stores, where does auth().protect() redirect them?

options.text: /signup
/dashboard/stores
/signin

questions.explanation: auth().protect() at src/middleware.ts lines 9-12 passes unauthenticatedUrl set to `${url.origin}/signin`. Unauthenticated visitors are sent to /signin; /dashboard/stores is the unauthorizedUrl used when a user is authenticated but lacks permission.

questions.prompt: What does the addToCart server action do when the cartId cookie points to a cart where closed = true?

options.text: Updates the existing cart row with the new item
Throws an error and returns it to the caller
Deletes the closed cart, inserts a new cart, and sets a fresh cartId cookie
Resets the closed flag to false and appends the item

questions.explanation: At src/lib/actions/cart.ts lines 189-206, when cart.closed is true the action calls db.delete(carts) on the old row, then db.insert(carts) with the new item, stores the returned id in the cartId cookie, and returns { data, error: null }. It never resets the closed flag.

evidence.note: closed-cart branch: delete then insert fresh cart + set cookie

questions.prompt: What is the return shape of every server action in this codebase on failure?

options.text: Throws an Error that the caller must catch
{ data: null, error: string }
{ success: false, message: string }
{ data: null, error: Error }

questions.explanation: src/lib/actions/cart.ts lines 231-235 show the canonical catch block: return { data: null, error: getErrorMessage(err) }. getErrorMessage() (src/lib/handle-error.ts) always returns a string. Actions never throw to callers, and there is no 'success' field or Error object in the return shape.

evidence.note: catch block returning { data: null, error: getErrorMessage(err) }

questions.prompt: After stripe.paymentIntents.create succeeds, where is the clientSecret stored so the browser can initialise Stripe Elements?

options.text: In a signed server-side session cookie
In the carts table row, paymentIntentId and clientSecret columns
In Upstash Redis with a TTL equal to the session expiry
In the orders table alongside the order total

questions.explanation: src/lib/actions/stripe.ts lines 518-524 show db.update(carts).set({ paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id, clientSecret: paymentIntent.client_secret }) after the PaymentIntent is created. The server component then reads this value back and passes it to CheckoutShell as a prop.

questions.prompt: Which Stripe event triggers the creation of address and order records in the database?

options.text: checkout.session.completed
payment_intent.processing
payment_intent.succeeded
charge.succeeded

questions.explanation: src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts lines 109-219 handle the 'payment_intent.succeeded' case. This branch inserts into addresses and orders, decrements product inventory, and marks the cart closed=true. The 'payment_intent.processing' case (line 105) only logs.

evidence.note: case 'payment_intent.processing' — only logs, no DB writes

questions.prompt: Before the addProduct server action inserts a row, what check does it perform?

options.text: Verifies the seller's Stripe account is connected
Checks whether another product in the store has the same name
Validates the uploaded image URLs against the UploadThing CDN domain
Confirms the seller's userId matches the storeId owner

questions.explanation: src/lib/actions/product.ts lines 63-72 query products for a row with eq(products.name, input.name) before inserting. If a match is found it throws 'Product name already taken.' The ownership check exists in updateProduct/deleteProduct (lines 97-100) but not in addProduct.

evidence.note: db.query.products.findFirst by name — duplicate name guard

questions.prompt: Which npm package is used as the PostgreSQL driver inside the Drizzle ORM setup in this project?

options.text: pg (node-postgres)
pg-promise
postgres (postgres-js)
@neondatabase/serverless

questions.explanation: src/db/index.ts lines 2-3 import drizzle from 'drizzle-orm/postgres-js' and postgres from 'postgres', then call postgres(env.DATABASE_URL). The 'pg' package is listed in package.json but Drizzle does not use it — postgres-js is the actual driver.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of takeFirstOrThrow() in src/db/utils.ts?

options.text: Wraps a Drizzle query in a try-catch and re-throws with a friendly message
Returns the first element of a result array, or throws if it is undefined
Asserts that a query returned exactly one row, throwing if more are found
Returns the first element of an array, or returns null if empty

questions.explanation: src/db/utils.ts lines 7-15 show takeFirstOrThrow<T>(items: T[]) calls takeFirst (items.at(0)), and throws 'First item not found' if the result is falsy. It does not check for multiple rows or return null — that is takeFirst's behaviour.

evidence.note: takeFirst returns at(0); takeFirstOrThrow throws if undefined

questions.prompt: What happens at application startup if DATABASE_URL is missing from the environment?

options.text: The app boots normally; the first DB query throws a connection error
A console warning is printed and the app falls back to SQLite
The @t3-oss/env-nextjs validation in src/env.js throws before the server starts
next build succeeds but next start exits with code 1

questions.explanation: src/env.js lines 1-76 use createEnv from @t3-oss/env-nextjs, which validates all server vars at import time. DATABASE_URL is a required server variable. A missing value causes validation to throw immediately — the server never reaches route handlers. SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1 bypasses this (for CI builds).
